chunks: Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar narrated from Ibrahim ibn Hashim, from Nuh ibn Shu'ayb, from Hariz, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, who said:

The junub and the menstruating woman may open the mushaf from behind a cloth, and may recite from the Qur'an whatever they wish except the sajdah; and they may enter the mosque while passing through, but they must not sit in it, and they must not approach the two sacred mosques.

key_terms.الثَّوْبِ: A cloth used here as a barrier when opening the mushaf.
key_terms.السَّجْدَةَ: The Qur'anic passage involving obligatory prostration that is excepted here.
key_terms.الْجُنُبُ: A person in the state of janabah requiring ghusl.
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدَيْنِ الْحَرَمَيْنِ: The two sacred mosques, al-Masjid al-Haram and al-Masjid al-Nabawi.
key_terms.الْمُصْحَفَ: The written copy of the Qur'an.

ai.seo_question: What are the rulings for a junub or menstruating woman regarding the mushaf, Qur'an recitation, and entering mosques?
ai.summary: This hadith states legal rulings concerning the junub and the menstruating woman regarding touching the mushaf, reciting the Qur'an, and entering mosques. It permits limited interaction with the Qur'an and passage through ordinary mosques, while restricting recitation of verses of sajdah and access to the two sacred mosques.
